# DSH Chat Import
**A session import plugin built on DeepSeek Harness: import conversation history from other agents w
ith one click, then keep talking in DeepSeek Harness.**
> **All sessions, continued in DSH.**
[](README.md) [](README.zh-CN.md)

## Usage
1. Import conversations from the GUI
Click the **Import sessions** button at the bottom of the left sidebar to open the import window. Wi
th the DSH Claude Style theme, that button lives in the account menu at the bottom left. Pick the co
nversations you want and import them in one click.
Rows carry their own tools: **double-click** a row to preview the conversation (a read-only dry-run
— plugin injections skipped, tool calls folded into one line), switch the search box to **In content
** to search message bodies instead of titles, **hide** a row reversibly, move a single-session sour
ce file to the Recycle Bin, or **drag the row onto a workspace** in the left sidebar to import it th
ere with its timestamps shifted so it sorts to the top. The exact rules are in docs/USAGE.md.
If the file came from somewhere else — a web-app export, a script you wrote, a tool this plugin does
not list — use **Import from file** at the top of the same window. Type a local path and press Ente
r, or press **Choose…** to pick files. When the path is a directory, it asks whether to search subfo
lders. Check the preview, then import. If detection fails, it lists why each candidate parser gave u
p and points you at the skill that converts the format.
> These screenshots also use the DeepSeek palette from DSH Claude Style, another theme plugin by the
same author. It recreates the look and feel of Claude Code Desktop inside DSH and ships two palette
s, one for Claude and one for DeepSeek. If the default theme is not quite your taste, give it a try.
The workspaces and sessions in the screenshots are sample data.
2. Import through an agent's tool call

Cursor workspace grouping and imports prefer the local Cursor workspace registry by conversation id,
accepting only existing directories. Imports always read fresh; discovery caches successful reads a
nd invalidates on DB/WAL changes. Malformed JSON and filesystem failures are counted in diagnostic w
arnings. When no usable entry exists, they fall back to decoding the transcript's project directory
gs. When no usable entry exists, they fall back to decoding the transcript's project directory name.
## Configuration
To accommodate TUI users, the tools this plugin provides start out injected into context. In Setting
s you can switch them to **not injected**, or to a partial injection, which saves a fair number of t
can switch them to **not injected**, or to a partial injection, which saves a fair number of tokens.
Full tool and command usage is in **docs/USAGE.md**.

## Features
| Capability | Entry Point | Description |
| Import | Sidebar panel, "Import" tab | Import conversations from other agents, keeping reasoning,

tool call results, and system prompts (optional) |
| Import from file | Panel "Import from file" / `
/import auto <path>` | Any local file or directory: three-level detection (explicit format > content
marker > parser trial), preview first, an optional search-subfolders prompt for directories, and, w
hen every parser fails, a ready-to-send agent task brief plus a registered `dsh-chat-import-convert`

skill |
| Retract Import | Sidebar panel, "History" tab | Review import history and delete sessions

this plugin created |
| Export | Context tool | Serialize DSH sessions back into other agents' form

ats |
| Ignore | Automatic, plus `/ignores` | Archiving, deleting, or removing a workspace registers
the source, so rescans skip it; `/ignore` and `/unignore` manage the table |
Codex discovery prefers the session title saved in `session_index.jsonl` (`thread_name`), so a renam
e made in Codex still shows up. Only when no indexed title exists does it fall back to the first rea
l user prompt, extracted the same way import does it, with injected page context excluded. The title
index is streamed line by line, and the last valid title record wins for each session.
For activity time, Codex discovery takes the latest valid timestamp found within bounded head and ta
il windows of the transcript and combines the results across rollout pages. File modification time i
s the fallback when the transcript carries no timestamp at all, so activity times still come back wh
en the host file service does not expose modification times. A timestamp inside a truncated record c
ile service does not expose modification times. A timestamp inside a truncated record can be missed.
